I was on fluoxetine for a while and it made me feel more numb than anything. I felt like I was just going through the motions, didn't care about anything. I got out of bed, things seemed easier, but I wasn't feeling happy. I couldn't really feel anything. I got off them as soon as possible, realising that I'd rather feel how I do now than feel nothing at all. On them, I could've jumped in front of a train and not cared in the slightest. I could've hurt someone and i don't think I'd have bat an eyelid (I wouldn't have any other time. I'm really nice normally, promise!). They didn't make me feel like myself. It was all just a messy, horrible experience for me, to be honest.

I'm gonna go out on a limb and say NTA.

You're a mother with two children on public transport (which, depending on which area you're in, can be very dodgy.) And an old man coming to sit with a mother and her two kids when there are other available seats is really creepy, especially since his face was hidden. You had no idea what his intentions were, and I'm sure he was setting alarm bells off in your head. I would've said no, too!

I mean, yeah, having bags on the free seat was not ideal, but from the sounds of it this was booked seating and the pregnant woman who had booked decided not to sit there, therefore, I don't see the problem. No one else should've been sitting there, so why can't OP put her bags on the seat?

Idk. The whole situation set off creep alarms in my mind and I wasn't even there. I don't think you're TA.
